summary: Update the docs, planner, and code-review capabilities so every primary human-facing artifact communicates its main idea visually and then supplies concise, precise text for humans and downstream agents. README work will use a compact repository-flow visual; planner folios will compare current and proposed architecture; code-review reports will visualize the review funnel and affected surface. Existing approval gates, strict machine-readable inputs, offline rendering, and harness parity remain intact.

components.name: Docs contract
components.purpose: Guides all harness-specific docs agents to write short, approachable READMEs with a durable visual explanation of the repository.

components.name: Planner sidecar and folio
components.purpose: Carries explicit current and proposed architecture sources and renders them as a before/after change story alongside dependency and risk detail.

components.name: Code-review renderer
components.purpose: Derives an always-present visual review topology and impact summary from the strictly validated review JSON.

components.name: Parity and regression gates
components.purpose: Keep Claude, Codex, and Antigravity instructions aligned and verify visuals remain accessible, offline, printable, and backed by textual detail.

issues.title: Define and enforce the visual-first README standard
issues.body: Update the docs skill and the Claude, Codex, and Antigravity docs-agent definitions with one consistent README contract. A README must lead with a plain-language statement of what the repository does, explain why it exists, provide the shortest viable quickstart, and include a compact visual of the primary architecture or workflow. Prefer GitHub-rendered Mermaid when relationships matter and a durable text diagram when Mermaid would add complexity; every visual needs a nearby textual explanation and meaningful labels so it remains understandable to screen readers, raw-Markdown readers, and agents. Keep prose concise, remove repetition, and do not invent a decorative diagram for information that is clearer as a small table. Add focused contract tests and a representative README fixture or reference example without turning docs_check into a brittle semantic linter for arbitrary repositories.

acceptanceTests.name: readme-contract-parity
acceptanceTests.oracle: All three harness-specific docs agents and the docs skill require the same what/why/quickstart/visual structure and concise human-friendly prose.

acceptanceTests.name: visual-has-textual-equivalent
acceptanceTests.oracle: The documented README example pairs its Mermaid or text diagram with labels and nearby prose that conveys the same repository flow without relying on rendered graphics.

acceptanceTests.name: docs-gate-remains-compatible
acceptanceTests.oracle: Existing clean sample repositories and the real repository still pass docs_check; arbitrary repositories are not rejected solely because semantic visual quality cannot be mechanically inferred.

issues.title: Make planner folios show the architectural change story
issues.body: Extend the planner's strict architecture contract and renderer so every plan contains a visual current-state and proposed-state comparison, not only a target diagram. Keep both diagram sources in the machine-readable sidecar, validate them before rendering, and present them with explicit Current and Proposed labels plus a concise textual explanation of the delta. Preserve the existing dependency graph, wave diagram, risks, approval gate, offline Mermaid bundle, source fallback, print behavior, deterministic naming, and GitHub reconciliation. Update examples and the planner contract so agents know to model the smallest meaningful system boundary and use a non-architectural state or data-flow comparison when the change is not structural.

acceptanceTests.name: requires-current-and-proposed-visuals
acceptanceTests.oracle: The strict sidecar validator rejects an architecture missing either the current-state or proposed-state Mermaid source and accepts a valid pair.

acceptanceTests.name: renders-labeled-comparison
acceptanceTests.oracle: The HTML folio renders distinct Current and Proposed visuals, preserves both source fallbacks, and includes concise textual change context without removing the other required sections.

acceptanceTests.name: planner-remains-offline-and-deterministic
acceptanceTests.oracle: Two renders of the same sidecar are byte-identical, load no external resources, print cleanly, and retain approval and reconciliation identity semantics.

issues.title: Add an always-present visual summary to code-review reports
issues.body: Add a compact, accessible visual to the self-contained code-review report that shows the path from selected lenses through raw candidates and independent verification to surviving findings and affected files. Derive it entirely from the existing strict review JSON and render context so the machine contract stays authoritative. The visual must remain meaningful for blocked, approve-with-nits, and zero-finding reviews; use semantic HTML and CSS or another fully inline technique with a nearby textual summary and print-safe fallback. Preserve ranked expandable findings, refuted-candidate evidence, filters, strict validation, deterministic output, and GitHub issue reconciliation. Update the skill report contract so the visual is mandatory and clarify that architecture before/after is appropriate only when review evidence supports it; the topology/impact view is the reliable default.

acceptanceTests.name: renders-review-topology
acceptanceTests.oracle: A populated review renders a labeled visual connecting lenses, candidate counts, verification outcome, severity, and affected files using only validated report data.

acceptanceTests.name: renders-clean-review-visual
acceptanceTests.oracle: An approved review with zero verified findings still renders an honest visual that communicates completed verification and no affected files, without empty or misleading nodes.

acceptanceTests.name: review-visual-is-accessible-offline-and-printable
acceptanceTests.oracle: The report has a textual equivalent and semantic labels, contains no external loads, remains deterministic, and exposes the visual meaning in print and without JavaScript.

issues.title: Document the visual communication contract and run the full skill suite
issues.body: After the three skill surfaces are implemented, update the repository README and changelog or handover material to describe the new output guarantees. Record an ADR if the implementation establishes a durable cross-skill rule about visual-plus-text equivalents. Verify shared report CSS parity remains byte-identical where required, generated examples demonstrate the behavior, all affected skill tests pass, docs_check passes, and no live harness instructions drift from the source skill contracts. Keep the repository README itself concise and use its own workflow visual as the dogfood example.

acceptanceTests.name: affected-skill-suites-pass
acceptanceTests.oracle: The docs, planner, and code-review unittest suites all pass together after the contract changes.

acceptanceTests.name: shared-report-style-parity
acceptanceTests.oracle: Planner and code-review shared report.css files remain byte-identical and their existing parity assertion passes.

acceptanceTests.name: repository-docs-demonstrate-standard
acceptanceTests.oracle: The root README gives a newcomer a concise what/why/quickstart explanation plus a visual workflow with a textual equivalent, and docs_check reports no violations.

risks.title: Visual requirements produce decorative noise
risks.mitigation: Require each visual to answer a named reader question, permit tables or text diagrams where they communicate better, and pair every visual with concise prose.

risks.title: Planner schema evolution breaks existing sidecars
risks.mitigation: Make the schema transition explicit, update fixtures and examples together, provide a clear validation error, and test the chosen compatibility behavior before release.

risks.title: Visual and textual representations drift
risks.mitigation: Derive report visuals and nearby summaries from the same validated data, and add assertions that both carry the same labels, counts, and states.

risks.title: Harness-specific docs instructions diverge
risks.mitigation: Add parity assertions covering the shared README contract across Claude, Codex, and Antigravity agent definitions.
